title: USP Booking
description: Booking lifecycle schema for the Universal Scheduling Protocol. Defines Booking, Buyer, BookingPayment, PaymentContext, Action, Message, and Cancellation objects.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: A scheduled service instance for a specific buyer at a specific time.

id.description: Unique booking identifier, generated by the business.

service_name.description: Service display name, captured at booking time. Snapshot that does not change if the service name is later updated.

buyer.description: The person making and paying for the booking. When no recipient is provided, the buyer is also the person receiving the service.

recipient.description: The person receiving the service, when different from the buyer (e.g., a parent booking for a child, an assistant booking for their employer, or a gift booking). When absent, the buyer is the recipient.

party_size.description: Total number of attendees. For appointment types typically 1. For group/reservation reflects spots booked.

resources.description: The specific resources assigned to this booking.

location.description: The business's location for this booking. Present when channel.type is at_business_location or hybrid. For at_buyer_location, see delivery_address instead.

delivery_address.description: The buyer's service delivery address, echoed back from the create-booking request. MUST be present when the service's channel.type is at_buyer_location. MAY be present for other channels (e.g. a hybrid service where the buyer chose the mobile option).

confirmation_mode.description: Reflects the service's confirmation policy at booking time.

payment.description: Payment state. MUST be present when requires_payment is true and payment_timing is at_booking or deposit_required.

actions.description: Ordered array of pending tasks the buyer must complete. MUST be present and non-empty when status is requires_action; MUST be absent or empty otherwise. The booking has status requires_action if and only if this array contains at least one action with status pending.

booking_url.description: Stable URL where the buyer can view and manage this booking. Provided by the business. Used in confirmation emails, calendar events, and buyer portals.

dispute.description: Present when a payment dispute has been opened for this booking.

messages.description: Soft messages from the business providing context about the booking state (e.g., manual confirmation pending, cancellation window closing). These are informational and do not block booking creation. MUST NOT be present for protocol errors — those are returned as HTTP error codes.

cancellation.description: Present when the booking has been canceled.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the booking was created.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last status change or modification.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiration time. Present for pending and requires_action bookings.

revision.description: OPTIONAL. Opaque concurrency token for the current state of this booking, used for conditional writes (specification.md Section 5.6). A business that returns this MUST honour a matching precondition on mutating operations - If-Match on REST, _meta.usp.if_match on MCP - and MUST reject a stale one rather than applying the write, which is what stops two agents holding the same booking_scoped_credential from silently clobbering each other. Its presence in a response IS the advertisement that the business supports conditional writes; a platform that receives no revision performs unconditional writes, exactly as with an absent HTTP ETag. The value MUST change whenever any part of the booking changes and MUST NOT be reused for a different state. Businesses SHOULD NOT derive it from updated_at alone, since two modifications inside one timestamp tick would collide and defeat the check. Platforms MUST treat it as opaque: do not parse it, order it, or infer recency from it - it may be a row version, an entity tag, or a hash.

SlotReference.title: SlotReference
SlotReference.description: Reference to a booked time slot.

Buyer.title: Buyer
Buyer.description: The person making and paying for the booking. When no separate recipient is specified, the buyer is also the person receiving the service.

consent.description: Optional buyer consent signals. Nested inside the buyer object per UCP convention.

DeliveryAddress.title: DeliveryAddress
DeliveryAddress.description: The buyer's service delivery address, used when the business travels to the buyer (channel.type: at_buyer_location). REQUIRED on POST /bookings when the booked service's channel.type is at_buyer_location; echoed back on the Booking object.

line2.description: Secondary address line (apartment, suite, unit, floor).

coordinates.description: Optional geocoded coordinates for dispatch and routing.

BuyerConsent.title: BuyerConsent
BuyerConsent.description: Declarative consent choices transmitted by the platform on behalf of the buyer. The protocol communicates consent but does not enforce it — legal compliance remains the business's responsibility.

analytics.description: Consent for the business to use booking data for analytics and service improvement.

marketing.description: Consent for the business to send marketing communications to the buyer.

preferences.description: Consent for the business to store and use buyer preferences (preferred resources, times, etc.).

sale_of_data.description: Consent for the business to sell or share buyer data with third parties.

health_data.description: USP-specific extension. Consent for processing health-related data (applicable to healthcare verticals). MUST comply with HIPAA/GDPR as applicable.

BookingPayment.title: BookingPayment
BookingPayment.description: Payment state within a booking. Tracks the lifecycle of payment.

amount.description: Service fee in minor currency units, before tax. REQUIRED when timing is at_booking or deposit_required. Does not include tax_amount.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. REQUIRED when amount is present.

amount_due.description: Amount due now in minor currency units. REQUIRED when timing is at_booking or deposit_required.

deposit_amount.description: The deposit amount in minor currency units. Present when timing is deposit_required.

tax_amount.description: Tax amount in minor currency units. When present, the total charged to the buyer is amount + tax_amount. MUST use the same currency as amount.

transaction_id.description: Transaction identifier from the payment provider. Set after payment is confirmed.

order_reference.description: External order identifier from the checkout system. Used for refund reconciliation.

PaymentContext.title: PaymentContext
PaymentContext.description: Universal payment handoff object nested inside a payment action. Contains everything a checkout system needs to process payment. The payment expiry deadline is carried on the action's expires_at field.

amount_due.description: Amount to collect in minor currency units.

item_id.description: Service ID for checkout system line item mapping.

line_items.description: Itemized breakdown for display and checkout integration.

tax_amount.description: Tax portion of amount_due in minor currency units. When present, the checkout system SHOULD display the tax breakdown. Pre-tax subtotal is amount_due minus tax_amount when tax_amount is present.

metadata.description: Machine-readable context for the checkout system to pass back during confirmation.

Action.title: Action
Action.description: A pending task the buyer must complete before a booking can be confirmed. Each action has a type, status, continue URL, and expiry.

continue_url.description: Business-hosted HTTPS URL for completing this specific action. MUST use the https:// scheme; platforms MUST reject non-HTTPS values. Valid only until expires_at; MUST reference server-side session state, not sensitive data in the query string.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline for this action. Can be equal to or earlier than the booking expiry.

payment_context.description: Payment handoff object. MUST be present when type is payment (Standalone Mode only).

Message.title: Message
Message.description: Message providing context about the booking state.

path.description: Optional JSON Pointer to the relevant field.

Cancellation.title: Cancellation
Cancellation.description: Cancellation details when a booking has been canceled.

fee.description: Cancellation fee in minor currency units.

refund_amount.description: Amount refunded in minor currency units.

Dispute.title: Dispute
Dispute.description: A payment dispute (chargeback) opened against a booking. Opening a dispute does NOT change payment.status — the payment remains in its current state (e.g., paid). Payment status MAY change to refunded or partially_refunded only if the dispute resolves in the buyer's favor.

status.description: Current dispute status. resolved_buyer: resolved in the buyer's favor (refund issued). resolved_business: resolved in the business's favor (no refund).

reason.description: Machine-readable reason code. Well-known values: service_not_provided, quality_issue, unauthorized, duplicate.

opened_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the dispute was opened.

resolved_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the dispute was resolved. Present only when status is resolved_buyer or resolved_business.

PostPaymentReturnRequest.title: PostPaymentReturnRequest
PostPaymentReturnRequest.description: Applicable when checkout_systems: redirect is in use. Instructs the business where to redirect the buyer's browser after payment completes, is cancelled, or is abandoned. The platform SHOULD always include this field on the redirect path — without it, the platform cannot predict or control where the buyer lands after the payment flow. The business MUST issue an HTTP GET redirect to url (with all params appended as URL query parameters) in both terminal outcomes: payment completed and payment cancelled/abandoned.

url.description: The platform's return URL. The business MUST redirect the buyer's browser to this URL (via HTTP GET) after payment completes, is cancelled, or is abandoned, appending any params as query parameters.

params.description: Query parameter key-value pairs the business MUST append verbatim to url when issuing the return redirect. Keys and values are opaque to the business — the platform uses them to carry whatever correlation state it needs (e.g. a token generated before the booking request) so it can map the returning buyer back to its session without relying on the booking_id (which is not yet known at request time).
